newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina has no plans for 20-yr peso bond - Kiguel.
newsitem.headline: Argentina has no plans for 20-yr peso bond - Kiguel.

text.p: Argentina has received offers to issue a 20-year peso-denominated bond in international markets but has no plans for such a placement now, a senior government official said.
"We have received offers but for now it does not fit into our financing program," Miguel Kiguel, Argentina's undersecretary of finance, told Reuters.
Rumors that Argentina was about to issue a 20-year peso-denominated bond circulated in the Brady bond market on Tuesday.
Argentina launched a 10-year 500 million peso Eurobond at the end of January. The issue was lead managed by J.P. Morgan.
Moody's Investors Service has a B1 rating on Argentina's sovereign local currency debt, the same rating as on its foreign currency debt.
